bib.title: Detecting Hallucinated Content in Conditional Neural Sequence Generation
bib.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL-IJCNLP 2021

read.skipped: The PDF has 12 pages and ends at the references; the appendices the text cites (A-E, Tabs 5, 7, 9) are not in the PDF, so hyperparameters in them are unavailable.

question: Can hallucinated tokens in conditional sequence generation output (MT, summarization) be detected at token level without reference text or human-labelled training data?
hypothesis: A pretrained LM fine-tuned on synthetic data with automatically inserted hallucinations will generalise to detect real hallucinations in model outputs.
contributions: A new task of token-level hallucination detection that needs no reference at test time
New human-annotated MT benchmark sets (Zh-En patent and COVID-19) plus processed XSUM annotations
A synthetic-data method (BART insertion, edit-distance labels) for fine-tuning XLM-R/RoBERTa detectors
Use of token labels for fine-grained loss in self-training and noisy-corpus MT, and for word-level QE

method.summary: Hallucinated targets T' are generated by noising the true target T and decoding with BART (no source access); tokens changed by edit distance are labelled 1. XLM-R (MT) or RoBERTa (summarization) is fine-tuned on (S,T,T') with a token classification loss plus MLM loss. Evaluated against human token labels, WMT18 word-level QE, and as a loss mask in self-training and corpus filtering.
method.task: token-level hallucination detection (sequence labelling) for MT and abstractive summarization

datasets.name: Zh-En multi-domain (Wang et al. 2020b) Dtrain
datasets.size: law 1.46M, news 1.54M, subtitles 1.77M sentences plus 870 patent sentences

datasets.name: MT hallucination eval Deval
datasets.size: 250 sentences: 150 patent test, 100 COVID-19 (Anastasopoulos et al. 2020)
datasets.source: new annotations by 3 bilingual annotators, majority vote

datasets.name: XSUM annotations (Maynez et al. 2020)
datasets.size: 500 articles sampled from XSUM test (226,711 articles) x 4 systems

datasets.name: WMT18 en-de word-level QE
datasets.size: 13,442 labeled parallel sentences, plus 50K unlabeled target sentences for unsupervised

datasets.name: CWMT2017 patent test
datasets.size: 1,500 sentences (full patent test); 2.9M unlabeled Chinese patent sentences for self-training

datasets.name: WMT19 low-resource corpus filtering
datasets.size: Ne-En 40.6M words, Si-En 59.6M words noisy; clean Ne-En 564K, Si-En 646K, Hi-En 1.6M
datasets.source: Koehn et al. 2019; Guzmán et al. 2019
datasets.preprocessing: top-scored 1M-10M English tokens selected with Chaudhary et al. 2019 scores

models.name: XLM-R
models.architecture: cross-lingual masked LM, fine-tuned as token classifier (MT, QE)

models.name: RoBERTa
models.architecture: monolingual masked LM, fine-tuned as token classifier (summarization)
models.context: 512 max input; average cutoff of 158 subwords from the source article

models.name: BART
models.architecture: 12 layer pretrained denoising seq2seq, used to generate T'

models.name: MBART
models.architecture: multilingual denoising seq2seq, fine-tuned on Dtrain

models.name: PtGen, TConvS2S, TranS2S, BERTS2S
models.architecture: XSUM summarizers from Maynez et al. 2020

training.objective: L = Lpred + alpha * Lmlm; Lpred is token classification over pseudo hallucination labels on T'; Lmlm on batches of (S,T) only
training.dropout: reference-token dropout in T: 0.5 summarization, 0.3 MT
training.regularisation: token dropout on T; alternative paraphrase targets via knowledge distillation (MT)

other.synthetic_noise: mask fraction pm ~ U[0,hm], random-replace prob pr ~ U[0,hr]; hm and hr are 0.6 and 0.3 (MT), 0.4 and 0.2 (summarization)
other.qe_unsupervised: synthetic data from 13,442 post-edited + 50K unlabeled target sentences
other.label_assignment: edit distance T' vs T; deletion and substitution positions in T' labelled 1
other.other_hyperparameters: deferred to Appendix B and C, not in this PDF

inference.decoding: BART synthetic generation: beam size 4, length penalty 3

parameters.self_training: token loss truncation drops losses on predicted hallucinated tokens; decoder HS masking masks decoder hidden states after cross-attention

metrics.name: F1 of token hallucination labels
metrics.definition: token-level F1 against majority-vote human labels

metrics.name: F1-Mult
metrics.definition: product of OK-F1 and BAD-F1 (WMT18 QE)

metrics.definition: tokenized BLEU and BLEURT for CWMT; SacreBLEU for WMT19 filtering

limits: Task is far from solved (authors); neural detector only slightly beats string/synonym baselines on XSUM, attributed to 512-token RoBERTa input truncating the article (avg 158 subwords cut).
MT annotation agreement only moderate (FK≈0.56); hallucination vs ungrammatical hard to separate.
Synthetic labels from edit distance are not guaranteed correct.
Intrinsic vs extrinsic not distinguished; under-generation not annotated.
Small MT eval set (250 sentences) in one language pair (Zh-En) and domain-shifted setting; summarization only XSUM, pre-LLM models.
Appendices (hyperparameters, ablations, full P/R) are absent from the supplied PDF.

terms.definition: any span gi..gi+j in G that is not supported by the source input S
a span in G consists of additional content without clear grounding in the input
a span of word(s) in G contains incorrect information due to synthesizing content using information present in S
